Playbook.name: Windows — Remote Service Execution via SMB Named Pipe (PsExec / Impacket) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A remote client accessed a service-execution named pipe (svcctl, PSEXESVC, atsvc) over SMB (5145), excluding scanners/machine accounts - the PsExec/Impacket remote-execution signature. Triage question: is this an attacker executing code remotely (lateral movement), or an approved remote-admin tool?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Remote service execution via SMB pipes is a primary lateral-movement technique; a confirmed instance usually means hands-on-keyboard movement.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the remote service-pipe access is lateral movement or an approved remote-admin tool.

Step.name: Who executed remotely, from where, on how many hosts
Step.Purpose: Fan-out across hosts via service pipes = lateral movement; a single admin action differs.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "5145" AND winlog.event_data.RelativeTargetName IN ("svcctl","PSEXESVC","atsvc") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS accesses = COUNT(*), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), host_list = VALUES(host.name), pipes = VALUES(winlog.event_data.RelativeTargetName) BY src, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | SORT accesses DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: One source hitting svcctl/PSEXESVC across many hosts = lateral movement. A management server doing this to a known set may be legitimate admin. PSEXESVC pipe specifically = PsExec.

Step.name: Was a service then installed / did the target run a shell
Step.Purpose: A new service (7045) or shell process on the target right after confirms remote code execution.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-*,logs-system.system-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("7045","4697","4688") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName, process.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A PSEXESVC/random service installed on the target right after the pipe access confirms execution - escalate to IR.

Node.Condition: Service-pipe access fan-out across hosts, or followed by service install/shell on the target.
Node.Result: True Positive (Lateral Movement via PsExec/Impacket - IR)

Node.Condition: A documented remote-admin/management tool performing expected remote service actions.
Single access by a plausible admin with no follow-on.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PSEXEC-WHO, INV-02-PSEXEC-EXEC to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the tool; baseline; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Attacker remote code execution / lateral movement.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate source and target; open IR; scope reached hosts.
Reset credentials used; remove installed services.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured admin tool using PsExec broadly.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
